Definition: of uncertain derivation; a live coal:--coal of fire.
BiblicalUsage: Paul tells the Romans to heap coals of fire on the head of an enemy by feeding him when he is hungry. The word is the live coal itself, the burning ember that the proverb turns into a picture of kindness.
TheologicalSignificance: One live coal in one proverb holds no doctrine of its own; its picture is Paul's, that kindness to an enemy burns hotter than revenge.
